title: Disney is paying $60 million to hire 66 Character.AI staffers
key_facts: Disney plans to pay $60 million per year to 66 Character.AI workers, according to a Chapter 11 filing on Tuesday (13 Oct 2026) from Character.AI's parent company.
Disney is also setting aside $30 million for an 'aggregate retention pool' and expects to spend $180 million on total compensation and retention over three years, the filing said.
Of the 66 offered jobs, 56 have already resigned from Character.AI; the other 10 await US government visa updates.
Disney also agreed to pay $20 million for key assets including some IP and technology; competing bids can be submitted by 20 November, overseen by a bankruptcy court judge.
Disney hired Character.AI chief executive Karandeep Anand in mid-September as its first company-wide tech chief; his pay is not disclosed.
The hiring came two weeks after Disney laid off several hundred workers, its third major round of layoffs since Josh D'Amaro became chief executive in mid-March.
Character.AI filed for bankruptcy after lawsuits from families alleging teenagers were harmed or died after using its chatbots; it and Google settled several child-safety suits earlier this year.
